headline: Discussed substance abuse and syringe disposal plans, health equity initiatives, problem properties, and public outreach strategies
summary: The board discussed ongoing work on a syringe disposal report, health equity initiatives including a new mobile health unit downtown, and city efforts on vacant and non-compliant properties. Members also discussed public outreach plans for mosquito-borne disease prevention, cataloging past outreach materials, and signage for railroad pesticide notifications. No formal votes were taken on these discussion items.
plain_text:
September 2, 2026 BOH draft minutes  
  
Board members participating: Chair Celia Bird, Jenny Tomczak, Jane Seymour and 
staffed by Health Officer Bill Ward.    
  
Board Chair Celia Bird called the meeting to order at 5:51 pm.   
  
Agenda   
Jenny made a motion to amend the agenda to remove the vote on item 4’s syringe report since 
Bianka would not be present at the meeting. Second by Jane.  Unanimous vote in favor.  Jenny 
then made a motion to approve the amended agenda, seconded by Jane.  Unanimous vote in 
favor.   
 
Draft minutes  
Celia asked that her comments about extreme heat and cooling centers be edited to only say 
that she started the outreach to other city staff and is hoping to have them attend a future 
Board Meeting.  Jenny made a motion to amend the minutes according to Celia’s suggestion 
and approve the minutes as amended.  2nd by Jane.  Vote was unanimous in favor. 
 
Public Forum     
There was one member of the public present, Ben Bosley who introduced himself as a 
Democratic candidate for Vermont House in Chittenden-15 (Burlington).  He said he was 
attending to better understand the Board is doing and the issues they believe deserve greater 
attention at the state level.  
 
Substance Abuse and Safe Syringe Disposal  
Celia suggested the group continue the discussion on work on Bianca's report on substance 
abuse and safe syringe disposal, with plans to reach out to city councilors to understand their 
needs and provide support for the safe syringe report review process. 
 
Bill discussed ongoing collaboration with the Peace and Justice Center, which will provide 
additional cleanup services for City Hall Park on Tuesday mornings to help address city staffing 
gaps on Mondays and Tuesdays.   Celia will reach out to Kason at the Peace and Justice Center 
about the syringe clean-up efforts and syringe drop box placement efforts. 
 
Health Equity  
Celia discussed the BOH health equity initiatives, focusing on serving vulnerable communities 
through substance abuse programs and translation services for diverse populations.  Bill 
highlighted a new mobile health unit deployed by UVM Medical Center in the downtown area 
to provide services to people who cannot easily access the hospital.   Bill will report back to the 
BOH on funding information after reaching out to the Fire Chief.
Problem Property update 
Bill gave an overview on vacant building compliance and public health initiatives.  He explained 
the city's efforts to address non-compliant properties, including monthly problem property 
meetings with department heads, increased fees and interest rates, and the potential for tax 
sales.  
 
Chair Report 
Celia reported on her communication with Victor Prusak, who's the Director of Engagement in K-12 
Registration for Burlington School District, about a draft playground design procedure.  The School 
District was interested in having the Board of Health look at it.  Celia will share the draft review with the 
board members for their thoughts.  
 
 Public Outreach/Communications  
The group discussed strategies for public outreach, including water safety and mosquito-borne 
disease prevention messaging.   Jane said she would repost previous health alerts on mosquito-
borne disease prevention.   Celia asked that we set up an organized system for cataloging past 
public outreach postings and budget documents for use in ongoing messages seasonally.  Bill 
will work with his administrative staff to organize this.   
 
Jenny asked about future railroad pesticide notifications and finding the best system to alert 
neighbors of the railroad when we get notifications from the State of Vermont that they have 
approved an application.  She asked that we consider an election campaign style sign that 
would be easy for the board to use when posting these multilingual signs along the railroad in 
the future.  Bill will work with DPW traffic staff who could produce signs for this effort.   
 
 Adjournment    
The next meeting was scheduled for September 30th at 5:45 PM. 
Jenny made a motion to adjourn the meeting, 2nd by Jane.  
Celia noted the meeting was adjourned at 6:51 p.m.
